subject: Insurance
title: Age: The Biggest Factor
description: A fast breakdown of Age: The Biggest Factor for builders.

hook.text: A 25-year-old pays $15/month for $500,000 term life. At 55, the same policy costs $150.

buildup.text: Every year you age, your risk of dying increases. Insurers adjust premiums to match rising mortality rates precisely.

discovery.text: Locking in a rate at a young age saves thousands. A 20-year term bought at 30 costs half of one bought at 40.

twist.text: After 70, term life becomes almost unaffordable. Insurers know the odds shift dramatically—and price accordingly.

climax.text: The best insurance advice is simple: buy young. Every year of delay costs more than the premium you skipped.

punchline.text: $15 at 25, $150 at 55. Life insurance gets expensive fast.

quiz.question: Why does life insurance cost more as you age?
